materials.text:
After a wet night, two containers in a garden may hold different amounts of water. It is tempting to call the fuller one evidence that more rain fell there. Recording the location helps someone judge those possible ____7____. The purpose is not to find the place that gives the largest number. It is to obtain a reading suited to the ____8____. A well-kept record states when the collection began and ended, because duration is another part of the ____9____. A single reading cannot describe every hour within that ____10____.

Several days of observations can reveal a pattern, provided the method remains comparable. Changes in equipment or position should be noted. They may explain an apparent shift that would otherwise be attributed to the ____11____. This does not make simple observations worthless. It makes their limits visible and their use more responsible. A pupil's garden record can be valuable without representing a whole town. The scale of the conclusion should match the scale of the ____12____. Good measurement joins a number to an account of what produced it. The rain in the container is real, but deciding what it ____13____ requires more than looking at the water. A question, a method and a record work ____14____.
